Who we are:

At Challenge Unlimited, our vision is to become a national leader in providing employment services to people with disabilities that empower them to reach their full potential. We intentionally provide opportunities for individuals with disabilities which will assist them to live, work, and participate in the community.

Challenge Unlimited is driven by its core values: community, helpfulness, abilities, leadership, learning, ethics, innovation, growth, and effective outcomes. It is these values that have powered Challenge Unlimited to its success and has helped over 600 disabled individuals find meaningful work across all of our locations.

Position Summary:

We are building a team of customer service representatives for a federal contact center that answers questions about FHA-insured home loans. The people who contact the center are homebuyers, homeowners, lenders, real estate agents, appraisers and housing counselors. They reach us by phone, email, chat, text and the web.
You will answer their questions using a knowledge base and a Salesforce case system. You will resolve most contacts on the first call, and you will pass the complex ones to federal housing specialists with complete notes. These positions depend on the award of a federal contract.

You will do well in this role if you have explained loans to borrowers and enjoyed that part of the job. You are patient on the phone, careful with details and comfortable following a procedure exactly. You also like a steady weekday schedule more than a sales quota.

We are interviewing now so that we can start qualified people as soon as the work begins. Applying now puts you first in line.

  • Location: Remote
  • Schedule: Monday to Friday, 8-hour shifts between 8:00am and 8:00pm eastern time.
  • Pay Rate: $23 - $24 per hour, depending on mortgage experience, plus benefits
Job Responsibilities:
  • Answer inbound calls, emails, chats and text messages from consumers and mortgage industry professionals about FHA mortgage programs.
  • Explain FHA loan programs, eligibility, the application process and where to find program guidance.
  • Help lenders, appraisers and other industry users with account access and system questions.
  • Find the answer in the knowledge base and HUD guidance, and give every caller the same accurate information.
  • Record every contact in Salesforce, and create and update service requests.
  • Transfer complex cases to the right HUD/FHA specialist with the full history attached.
  • Process inbound mail requests and send out booklets, forms and other program literature.
  • Help homeowners who call under stress, including after a natural disaster or a financial hardship, with patience and discretion.
  • Protect the personal and financial information of every caller under federal privacy and security rules.
  • Meet quality targets for first contact resolution, accuracy and response time, and take part in regular coaching.
  • Complete the required HUD security, privacy and program training each year.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Education: High school diploma or GED, two or more years of college, or an associate degree or higher preferred
  • Experience:
    • At least two years of customer service experience by phone. Experience with email and chat as well is preferred.
    • Clear written and spoken English. You will take a short writing test.
    • Computer skills, web research skills and typing of at least 40 words per minute.
    • The ability to pass a federal background check and a public trust investigation before you start.
  • Certifications/Licenses: Clear written and spoken English. You will take a short writing test.
  • Computer Skills: Computer skills, web research skills and typing of at least 40 words per minute.
  • Background Checks: The ability to pass a federal background check and a public trust investigation before you start.

What are we looking for most:

Most of the people we hire for this team will have a mortgage or real estate background. If this describes you, tell us about it in your application.
  • Three or more years of mortgage or real estate experience. Examples are loan officer, loan processor, underwriter, closer, post-closing, mortgage servicing, loss mitigation, mortgage call center, title and escrow, or licensed real estate agent.
  • Working knowledge of FHA loans. Knowledge of VA, USDA or conventional loans also helps.
  • A current or past NMLS license is a plus.
  • Spanish and English fluency is a plus.
  • Experience with Salesforce or another case management system is a plus.

raw.title: Product Manager - AI Platform
raw.excerpt: The bright side of mortgages nesto is Canada’s leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get-go — with total transparency and no haggling.
raw.description:
The bright side of mortgages

nesto is Canada’s leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get-go — with total transparency and no haggling.

About Us

As Canada's pioneer in online mortgage lending, nesto is transforming the way Canadians finance their homes. Our mission is to offer a positive, empowering, and transparent property financing experience, simplified from start to finish.

Borrowers benefit from rates that are often lower than those offered by the big banks, along with an exceptional end-to-end mortgage experience powered by best-in-class AI technology. Fast, simple, and fully digital, nesto has been recognized as CLA Lender of the Year for three consecutive years. That's the bright side of mortgages.

Nesto Group

Nesto Group is Canada's leading provider of mortgage technology and financing solutions, with more than CAD $80 billion in residential and commercial mortgages under administration. Trusted by many of the country's leading financial institutions, we combine over 50 years of mortgage expertise with proprietary cloud and AI technology to transform the future of lending.

Powered by our proprietary cloud and AI technology, nesto has become one of Canada's fastest-growing mortgage lenders, gaining market share across direct-to-consumer (D2C) residential lending, the broker channel, and multi-family commercial lending. Recognized as one of Deloitte's Fast 50 companies for three consecutive years, we continue to push the industry forward through innovation, technology, and customer-focused solutions.

Operating through our family of brands—CMLS, nesto, and Nesto Cloud—our mission is to build Canada's mortgage ecosystem of the future and create a true Canadian champion in lending technology and financial services. Learn more at:

Life at nesto

At nesto, we're passionate about challenging the status quo and building a better mortgage experience and saving money on their mortgages for Canadians. We foster a culture of collaboration, transparency, and creativity where every team member is empowered to take ownership, make an impact, and grow. If you're looking to solve meaningful problems alongside ambitious, supportive teammates, you'll feel right at home here.

About the role

At nesto, we are building Maestro: an AI platform that makes mortgage professionals dramatically more productive across sales, underwriting, and loan servicing. This is not "AI theater"— Maestro is already live, actively assisting underwriters with real files today.

As the Product Manager for the AI Platform, you will help turn this early proof-of-concept into the platform that defines AI-augmented lending in Canada. You will sit at the intersection of complex operational workflows, machine learning, and real mortgage expertise to turn hard problems into shipped product.

Why nesto’s approach to AI is different:

  • We sit where the work happens: We have direct access to the workflows, policies, and expert feedback inside real mortgage operations across the full lending journey.
  • Built for a regulated industry: Most AI companies build isolated demos or point solutions. We embed AI directly into production, continuously learning from human underwriter judgment.
  • End-to-end integration: We don't just solve one piece of the puzzle; we connect the full lending stack to make AI practically and systemically useful.

What you'll be doing here

  • Turn complex operational reality into clear PRDs, decision logic, and shipped product
  • Work closely with ML, engineering, underwriting ops, and business stakeholders to define and deliver the roadmap
  • Define and improve the metrics that matter: throughput, time-to-decision, accuracy, and capacity gained
  • Build tight feedback loops between AI output and expert human judgment
  • Keep execution moving in a high-ambiguity, high-accountability environment
  • Stay ahead of how AI is reshaping mortgage origination and bring informed recommendations to the roadmap
  • Share what you discover — how you work should make the people around you better

Who we're looking for

The profile.

  • 3-5 years of experience in consulting or a high-ownership product role in a complex environment
  • Ability to write clearly, think structurally, and go deep on systems, data, and edge cases
  • Comfortable operating without perfect inputs — you find the truth, make the call, and drive the work forward
  • Proven, active fluency with AI tools across your PM workflow: discovery, testing, documentation, analysis, and measurement.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex concepts clearly to non-experts in Product and Engineering

Preferred but not a must

  • Mortgage or regulated financial services experience — curiosity, rigor, and execution matter more
  • Familiarity with LOS systems, origination platforms, or lending technology
  • Exposure to AI or ML-assisted decisioning, document intelligence, or automation in a financial services context
  • Familiarity with broker and advisor-facing workflows and the nuances of supported versus self-serve client journeys

Interview process

How we get to know each other.

  • Recruiter Screen – 30 minutes
  • Discovery Call with Director of Product – 30 minutes
  • Take-home Assignment followed by Presentation and Q&A – 60 minutes
  • Final Stakeholder Interview – 45 minutes
  • Criminal Record and Reference Checks + Offer

Why You'll Love Working Here

We believe great people do their best work when they're supported professionally, personally, and financially. That's why we offer a comprehensive rewards package designed to help you thrive at every stage of your career.

  • Competitive Rewards — Competitive compensation, performance incentives (where applicable), and recognition for your contributions.
  • Health & Wellness — Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, Health & Wellness Spending Accounts (where applicable), telemedicine, Employee Assistance Programs, and mental health support for you and your family.
  • Time to Recharge — Generous vacation (4 weeks), floater days, and statutory holidays to help you recharge.
  • Planning for the Future — RRSP matching to support your long-term financial wellbeing.
  • Family Support — Enhanced maternity and parental leave top-up programs.
  • Learning & Growth — Education assistance, mentorship, training, and opportunities to build your career across Nesto Group.
  • Tools for Success — Modern technology, collaborative teams, and the resources you need to do your best work.


Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At Nesto Group, we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to succeed.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis), persons with disabilities, members of racialized communities, women, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.

If you require accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process, we are committed to working with you to meet your needs.

raw.description:
Grow our AI image service.

The role

We are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency. We are hiring one person who is good at deciding. Our AI image service is our fastest-growing service, and whichever area you own, you will be helping it grow.

You will own one named area. Which one is decided during the trial rather than now, based on what you turn out to be strong at. It will be one of these two:

  1. The hiring machine. How we find, screen and hire people. Running the funnel end to end, sourcing, chasing, scheduling, keeping our tracker honest, and telling us when the process itself is broken.
  2. Client delivery operations. How work gets planned, briefed, chased and shipped for our clients. Holding timelines, briefing the team properly, and making sure nothing quietly stalls.

Both are the same job underneath: you notice what has slipped, you decide what to do, and you close it without being asked.

This is not an assistant job and it is not a coordinator job. You will make real calls every day, and you will be judged on the quality of those calls rather than on how much you got through.

We are building a team of people who decide well without being managed. If you want to be told what to do each morning, this job is not for you.

What we are looking for

  1. You make decisions and you own them, including the ones that go wrong.
  2. You can tell which calls are yours and which are not, and you get that split right in both directions.
  3. You take feedback as information and change, without folding on something you have good reason to believe.
  4. You get better fast. We would rather have someone at seventy percent climbing than someone flat at eighty five.
  5. You spot when something is failing and say so, including when it is our process and not your work.
  6. You write clearly and honestly, especially about problems.

On experience

We do not ask for a number of years and we do not screen on your CV, because we decide on what you do in the trial.

Whatever employment you do list, we verify: employer, dates, title and paid status, evidenced by contract and payslips, in one exchange. You need to have held a full-time job at some point in the last 12 months. Beyond that there is no minimum, and a short history costs you nothing here. Misrepresenting the history you do have is disqualifying. Tell us the true version and you will not be penalised for it.

How the process works, and we tell you all of it now

  1. Application with a short Loom video.
  2. A short written step: your internet speed, your computer, and a few questions in your own words.
  3. Aptitude tests, with a published floor.
  4. A recorded video interview. One take, no re-records. We verify the work history you've told us about.
  5. A short call with the founder.
  6. A paid trial of six to eight weeks doing the real job.

The trial is where the decision actually gets made, including which of the two areas you end up owning. From the first week you will be making calls on live work, and we will tell you straight how each one landed. It is paid from day one: half rate for the first two weeks while you find your feet, full rate from week three onward, and a completion payment when you finish the trial, whether or not we hire you. If we stop early, you are paid for the days you worked.

Requirements

    1. Full time once hired, and this is your only job. During the paid trial you work 4 hours a day with us, 2 of them at a fixed time inside our working day, and you can keep your current job. If you pass, you give notice and join us full time within 30 days.
    2. Reliable internet, at least 30 Mbps down and 5 Mbps up, tested live with us.
    3. Strong written English.
    4. Based in Romania.
    5. You track your working time with our time tracking tool from day one.

Benefits

1500 USD per month on hire, set by responsibility and demonstrated capability, not by how long you have worked.

Pass your 90-day review and your pay goes up by 50 percent. The 90 days count from the day you start full time.

On top of that:

  1. A one-month annual bonus.
  2. 15 days of paid leave a year, rising with tenure, plus your own country's public holidays.
  3. Paid sick leave.
  4. A health allowance.
  5. A coworking allowance.

Responsibility and pay move quickly here for people who earn them. Authority over decisions that reach a client moves slowly and deliberately, and it is earned on a track record rather than on a good first month. We would rather tell you that now than have you discover it in month two.

About Ema

Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Employees take on the busy work across the employee experience, from recruiting, onboarding and benefits to IT support, invoice processing and payroll, so people can spend their time on work that needs them. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs.

We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Leader to manage and scale multiple product lines in the Voice, BPO, and Workforce Management space. This is a high-impact leadership role that sits at the intersection of real-time voice systems, operations research, and data-intensive platform engineering.

You will report directly to the Head of Engineering and own the engineering organization that builds the infrastructure powering Ema’s Voice AI Employees, Agent QA, auto-learning pipelines, rich analytics, and workforce optimization capabilities — all operating as scalable, multi-tenant systems deployed across global geographies.

You will collaborate with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to translate customer needs into production systems that handle high volumes of voice data, deliver real-time insights, and continuously improve through automated learning loops. As the owner of multiple product lines, you will balance roadmap priorities across Voice, BPO operations, and WFM (work force management) — ensuring each product evolves cohesively while meeting distinct customer needs.

What You Will Do

Scalable Multi-Tenant Systems

  • Architect and build multi-tenant systems that serve enterprise customers across geographies with strict data residency, isolation, and compliance requirements.

  • Design high-throughput ingestion systems capable of processing large volumes of voice data, call metadata, and operational telemetry in near real-time.

  • Make foundational architectural decisions on data stores, stream processing, and storage tiers — balancing query performance, cost, and operational simplicity.

  • Champion SOLID principles, clean architecture, and engineering rigor across all codebases — ensuring systems are testable, extensible, and maintainable at scale.

Team Building & Engineering Culture

  • Recruit, hire, and develop senior engineers across a multi-disciplinary function spanning voice engineering, backend systems, data engineering, and applied operations research.

  • Establish engineering standards, code review culture, and a strong bias toward shipping — with equal commitment to system reliability and customer experience.

  • Coach and grow senior/staff engineers into technical leaders; manage engineering managers as the organization scales.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to ensure the platform evolves in lockstep with customer needs and market feedback.

Voice Platform & Agent QA

  • Own the end-to-end engineering for Ema’s AgentQA capabilities — real-time voice pipelines, telephony integrations, and voice-to-action workflows.

  • Build and scale the Agent QA platform: automated call scoring, compliance monitoring, sentiment analysis, and coaching feedback loops.

  • Design auto-learning systems that continuously improve voice agents from production interactions — closed-loop feedback, model retraining triggers, and quality regression detection.

  • Deliver rich voice analytics: call volume trends, handle time distributions, first-call resolution metrics, agent performance dashboards, and anomaly detection.

  • Build scalable voice pipeline across geographies – keeping in mind PII, security and compliance requirements.

Workforce Management & Operations Research

  • Build WFM capabilities including demand forecasting, shift scheduling, real-time adherence monitoring, and capacity planning — applying operations research techniques to optimize workforce utilization.

  • Design and implement optimization algorithms for headcount modeling, skill-based routing, and workload balancing across multi-site, multi-timezone contact center operations.

  • Partner with ML/AI teams to integrate predictive models for call volume forecasting, attrition risk, and staffing efficiency.

What We Look For

Required

  • 12+ years of software engineering experience, with 4+ years leading engineering teams of 8+ engineers at high-growth startups or top-tier tech companies.

  • Deep expertise in building real-time, data-intensive systems.

  • Strong foundation in data stores and storage systems: relational databases, time-series stores, columnar analytics engines, and caching layers — with the judgment to choose the right tool for the workload.

  • Experience building quality software using AI-driven tools and workflows.

  • Track record of taking products from 0→1 and iterating rapidly based on customer feedback.

  • Hands-on proficiency with SOLID principles, clean architecture, and design patterns — you write and review production code and lead by example on system design.

  • Experience building scalable multi-tenant SaaS platforms with data isolation, geo-distributed deployments, and compliance requirements (SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA).

  • Track record of building ingestion systems for high volumes of load — event-driven architectures, stream processing (Kafka, Flink, or equivalent), and batch/real-time hybrid pipelines.

  • Strong product sense: ability to deeply understand customer problems in contact center, voice, and workforce domains and translate them into clean technical solutions.

  • Proven ability to hire, develop, and retain high-caliber engineers across multiple disciplines in competitive markets.

Good to have

  • Experience in voice/telephony systems: WebRTC, SIP, voice-over-IP infrastructure, or contact center platforms.

  • Background in operations research or optimization: scheduling algorithms, linear/integer programming, constraint satisfaction, or demand forecasting models.

  • Experience building analytics platforms: OLAP systems, real-time dashboards, metric computation engines, or BI infrastructure.

  • Prior work on auto-learning or continuous improvement systems: feedback loops from production data, automated retraining pipelines, or quality monitoring systems.

  • Experience with AI/ML-powered products in enterprise settings — agentic automation, LLM orchestration, or AI-driven UX.

  • Familiarity with WFM or contact center operations — staffing models, Erlang-based capacity planning, or real-time adherence systems.

Why Ema

  • Build at the intersection of Voice AI, operations research, and enterprise-scale systems — a rare combination of deeply technical challenges with direct customer impact.

  • Shape the engineering foundation of a category-defining AI platform — your architectural decisions will power how the world’s largest enterprises run their voice and workforce operations.

  • High-impact, high-visibility role with direct access to the Head of Engineering, co-founders, and enterprise customers.

  • A team of exceptional engineers from Google, Meta, Microsoft Research, and top CS programs worldwide.

  • Competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and the opportunity to build something that matters.

Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits.

Location: Remote

Who we are:

US Health Partners (“USHP”) seeks to redefine high-quality specialty care in the United States and establish a high-performing, technology-enabled care delivery platform. USHP is partnering with the country's leading physicians to build a comprehensive, out-patient focused specialty care network targeting the nation's cardiovascular concerns. Our physician-led organization is passionate about supporting exceptional care and enriching the lives of patients across the United States. We envision the opportunity to create a scaled, cutting-edge, technology-enabled healthcare services platform that leverages a value-based delivery model.

Position Summary:

The FP&A Analyst is an experienced contributor to the finance team, playing a key role in the company's budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting processes. This role independently builds and maintains financial models, monitors performance against budget, and delivers polished reporting and analysis that inform leadership decision-making. This is a strong opportunity for an experienced finance professional to deepen their FP&A expertise and take on greater ownership within a growing, physician-led healthcare organization.

Budgeting and Forecasting:

  • -Consolidate and validate inputs from cross-functional departments, ensuring accuracy and alignment with corporate goals.
  • -Track actual performance against budget and forecast, identify variances, and develop clear explanations and recommendations for leadership.

Financial Reporting and Analysis:

  • -Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports, including income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements.
  • -Independently conduct financial analysis to identify trends, variances, and opportunities for improvement, and translate findings into actionable insights.
  • -Build and maintain supporting schedules, dashboards, and executive-ready summaries for leadership review.
  • -Prepare revenue recognition reports as part of the close process, ensuring accurate accruals, cutoffs, and reconciliations across all practices.

Business Partnering:

  • -Serve as a day-to-day finance partner to assigned business units, providing financial insights and guidance to support decision-making.
  • -Proactively respond to data requests from business units and anticipate follow-on questions from leadership.
  • -Lead scenario analysis and ad hoc financial calculations to support business decisions and investment discussions.

Process Improvement:

  • -Identify and lead opportunities to streamline financial models, reports, and recurring processes.
  • -Maintain data integrity and consistency across financial systems and reporting tools, and recommend improvements where gaps are identified.
  • -Document and continuously improve FP&A processes and procedures, and help train junior team members on best practices.

Ad-hoc Analysis:

  • -Lead ad-hoc financial analysis and reporting as requested by the FP&A team or senior management.
  • -Provide analytical support for special projects, business initiatives, and cross-functional strategic efforts as needed.

Minimum Qualifications:

Education:

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

Experience:

  • -3–5 years of experience in FP&A, financial analysis, accounting, or a related role; healthcare or multi-site company experience is a plus.
  • -Solid understanding of financial modeling, forecasting, and budgeting techniques, with demonstrated ability to work independently.
  • -Strong proficiency with Excel; experience with financial planning tools or ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle, NetSuite) is a plus.

Competencies:

  • -Strong analytical skills with the ability to synthesize large, complex data sets into clear, actionable insights.
  • -Confident written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present financial information to non-financial stakeholders.
  • -Detail-oriented with a high level of accuracy and the ability to independently manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • -Strong business acumen and the ability to build effective working relationships across cross-functional teams.
  • -Experience with business intelligence (BI) tools and data visualization software (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) is a plus.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, use hands and fingers to handle or feel, as well as talk and hear. The employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is required to stand and walk. The employee may lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

Bilingual Medical Scheduling & Patient Support Specialist

Remote | Gastroenterology | Part-Time, 40 hours/week | Rate: $6.5/hour

About the Role

This Gastroenterology practice is looking for a highly organized, patient-focused Bilingual Medical Scheduling & Patient Support Specialist to support its clinics in two locations in Texas.

This role is heavily focused on appointment scheduling and patient communication, with a high daily call volume of approximately 70 to 90 calls per day. The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a fast-paced healthcare environment, managing multiple communication channels, and maintaining accurate patient documentation.

Key Responsibilities

1. Appointment Scheduling

  • Handle approximately 70 to 90 inbound and outbound calls daily related to appointments for the Lewisville and Denton locations.

  • Schedule, reschedule, and cancel patient appointments while ensuring accurate and timely communication with patients.

  • Maintain and update provider schedules in RingCentral and eClinicalWorks (eCW) based on availability and scheduling requirements.

2. Fax Management

  • Send and receive faxes involving patient records, referrals, insurance documents, and other clinical or administrative information.

  • Review incoming fax communications and route documents to the appropriate provider, department, or patient record.

  • Accurately log, upload, and organize faxed documentation within the clinic's systems.

3. Language Interpretation Support

  • Provide occasional language interpretation assistance between patients and clinic staff when needed.

  • Help ensure medical and administrative information is communicated clearly and accurately across language barriers.

  • Maintain professionalism, confidentiality, and accuracy when assisting with patient-provider communication.

4. Outbound Calling

  • Conduct outbound calls for appointment reminders, follow-ups, patient updates, and care coordination.

  • Contact insurance companies, referring providers, pharmacies, or other healthcare offices when necessary.

  • Document call outcomes, follow-up requirements, and relevant information accurately in the patient's record.

5. Patient Text Messaging

  • Send appointment confirmations, reminders, updates, and other approved patient communications through text messaging.

  • Monitor and collect patient responses and escalate questions or concerns to the appropriate clinic team member when needed.

  • Document relevant text conversations and patient responses in RingCentral and eCW to maintain continuity of care.

6. Billing and Payment Reminder Support

  • Contact patients regarding outstanding balances, billing reminders, or upcoming payment obligations as instructed by the clinic.

  • Provide basic payment-related information and direct patients to the appropriate billing resource when additional assistance is required.

Qualifications

  • Previous experience in medical administration, medical virtual assistance, patient scheduling, front desk support, or a similar healthcare role is strongly preferred.

  • Comfortable handling a high-volume call environment, including approximately 70 to 90 calls per day.

  • Experience using eClinicalWorks (eCW) and RingCentral is highly preferred.

  • Strong verbal and written English communication skills with a professional and patient-friendly approach.

  • Strong attention to detail, organization, documentation, and ability to manage multiple tasks throughout the workday.

  • Experience supporting a gastroenterology or specialty medical practice is an advantage.

  • Ability to communicate in an additional language and provide interpretation support is an advantage.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is confident speaking with patients throughout the day, comfortable managing a high volume of appointments and communications, and able to stay organized while supporting two clinic locations. You should be dependable, detail-oriented, professional, and capable of providing a positive patient experience while maintaining accurate documentation.

ABOUT KLED

Kled is building the largest opt-in human data network in the world.

We are not a labeling firm. We are not a task marketplace.

We are a consumer application where people upload their real photos, videos, and documents and get paid continuously.

We then filter, standardize, and license that data to frontier AI labs and enterprises that need fresh, rights-aware training data.

Since launching our mobile app in 2026, we have:

• Reached #1 on the App Store (Finance) with 0 paid marketing
• Scaled to 600,000+ active data contributors

• Processed 5M uploads per day

• Raised $15M+ from investors behind SpaceX, Airbnb, Coinbase, xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Spotify, Lyft, Uber, and more

Our mission is to let anyone download the app and earn a real living wage from uploading their data.

This listing is for one paid task in the Kled app: "Transit Departure Boards". There is no interview and no minimum hours: download the app, open the task, and you are paid per accepted submission.

What you will do

Photograph departure boards and timetables, bus, train, ferry, airport, or a printed schedule on a wall.

Steps

  1. Photograph the departure board or timetable

  2. Hold steady so the display is not smeared

  3. Upload

What gets rejected

  • Do not send heavily smeared shots

  • Do not crop off the header row

  • No people in frame

Accepted: Display or timetable readable, including LED and dot-matrix boards.

Pay

$0.30 per accepted photo. At a typical pace of about 1 minute per photo, that is about $18 per hour. A 20-minute session of about 20 photos pays about $6.00. Up to 50 photos per upload. You are paid per accepted submission (piecework, independent contractor); submissions that break the rules are not paid. Payouts are made in the app (PayPal, Venmo or a Solana wallet).

Where and when

Open in 11 Southeast Asian countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position.

What you need

  • An iPhone running iOS 18.6 or later (the Kled app is iPhone-only right now)

  • 18 or older

  • Your phone camera, used inside the Kled app

How to start

  1. Download Kled from the App Store: (also at kled.ai/app).

  2. Create your account and open Tasks.

  3. Search "Transit Departure Boards", read the brief and follow the on-screen steps.

  4. Submit. Accepted submissions are paid in the app.

Every submission is reviewed, and you opt in to a commercial training license on each upload; accepted submissions are licensed to AI labs. Questions: .

LOCATION: Remote

Career Team is looking to hire a Quality Assurance Supervisor who will be responsible for conducting case file reviews, monitoring data integrity, reviewing and approving payments, and ensuring program compliance with contract requirements. About the role

You will own merchant onboarding at Loop from sales handoff to Success handover, across three regions. You will lead a team of Onboarding Specialists, set the operating standard for every onboarding, and be accountable for time to go live, onboarding quality, and early churn. This role is about building a predictable onboarding engine that scales with our growth. It is not about running onboardings yourself.

What you will own

Onboarding Delivery and Governance

  • Own end to end onboarding performance: kickoff SLAs, milestone adherence, and go live dates across the full merchant portfolio.
  • Set the standards for kickoff, weekly touchpoints, configuration, migration validation and handover, and audit adherence.
  • Step in personally on strategic, high value or at risk merchants.

Cross Functional Partnership

  • Act as the primary escalation point for Sales, Implementation Engineering, Migration, Product and Success.
  • Improve the sales to onboarding handoff so merchants are scoped correctly before kickoff.
  • Agree SLAs and escalation paths with Implementation Engineering and Migration, and hold all sides to them.
  • Turn recurring merchant feedback into prioritised product inputs and track them to resolution.

Process, Tooling and Reporting

  • Own onboarding playbooks, templates and documentation standards.
  • Keep Salesforce, Sheets and internal dashboards accurate, and remove manual tracking wherever possible.
  • Report weekly and monthly on onboarding health to leadership, with risks and corrective actions.
  • Identify bottlenecks using data and redesign the process to remove them.

Merchant Experience and Retention

  • Own the merchant experience during onboarding, including handling of delays, product gaps and escalations.
  • Drive down churn during onboarding and in the first 30 days post handover.
  • Ensure every handover to Success is complete, documented and accepted by the Success team.

Team Leadership and Capacity

  • Lead, coach and grow a team of Onboarding Specialists across regions
  • Plan capacity and allocate merchants by region, complexity and specialist bandwidth.
  • Hire, onboard and ramp new specialists. Set clear performance goals and run regular 1:1s and reviews.

What we are looking for

  • 7+ years in customer onboarding, implementation or customer success at a B2B SaaS company, with 3+ years managing teams of 10 or more.
  • Experience leading distributed teams across multiple regions and time zones.
  • Strong track record of running onboarding at scale with measurable improvement in time to value and early retention.
  • Comfort with technical setups: integrations, data migration, configuration. You do not need to code, but you need to hold your own with engineers.
  • Hands on with Salesforce and dashboarding; data driven in how you run the team.
  • Calm, clear communicator in escalations with merchants and senior internal stakeholders.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's Telematics Business Unit — the company's oldest business line and the core of its revenue — is looking for a Principal Product Manager to take on a highly strategic, commercially-oriented mandate that cuts across the entire BU. In this role, you'll move fluidly between influencing company-wide strategic initiatives and hands-on building with engineering, reporting directly to the leader of the Telematics Business Unit.

This role exists to drive two things in parallel: step-function improvement in the core telematics business, and new, adjacent product bets that grow out of our core vehicle gateway (VG) products. You'll act as a single-threaded owner on cross-cutting initiatives forming your own hypotheses and business cases, then building and shipping alongside engineering to prove them out.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US, based in the Eastern Time Zone.

raw.title: Operations Associate (Hiring or Client Delivery)
raw.excerpt: Grow our AI image service. The roleWe are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency.
raw.description:
Grow our AI image service.

The role

We are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency. We are hiring one person who is good at deciding. Our AI image service is our fastest-growing service, and whichever area you own, you will be helping it grow.

You will own one named area. Which one is decided during the trial rather than now, based on what you turn out to be strong at. It will be one of these two:

  1. The hiring machine. How we find, screen and hire people. Running the funnel end to end, sourcing, chasing, scheduling, keeping our tracker honest, and telling us when the process itself is broken.
  2. Client delivery operations. How work gets planned, briefed, chased and shipped for our clients. Holding timelines, briefing the team properly, and making sure nothing quietly stalls.

Both are the same job underneath: you notice what has slipped, you decide what to do, and you close it without being asked.

This is not an assistant job and it is not a coordinator job. You will make real calls every day, and you will be judged on the quality of those calls rather than on how much you got through.

We are building a team of people who decide well without being managed. If you want to be told what to do each morning, this job is not for you.

What we are looking for

  1. You make decisions and you own them, including the ones that go wrong.
  2. You can tell which calls are yours and which are not, and you get that split right in both directions.
  3. You take feedback as information and change, without folding on something you have good reason to believe.
  4. You get better fast. We would rather have someone at seventy percent climbing than someone flat at eighty five.
  5. You spot when something is failing and say so, including when it is our process and not your work.
  6. You write clearly and honestly, especially about problems.

On experience

We do not ask for a number of years and we do not screen on your CV, because we decide on what you do in the trial.

Whatever employment you do list, we verify: employer, dates, title and paid status, evidenced by contract and payslips, in one exchange. You need to have held a full-time job at some point in the last 12 months. Beyond that there is no minimum, and a short history costs you nothing here. Misrepresenting the history you do have is disqualifying. Tell us the true version and you will not be penalised for it.

How the process works, and we tell you all of it now

  1. Application with a short Loom video.
  2. A short written step: your internet speed, your computer, and a few questions in your own words.
  3. Aptitude tests, with a published floor.
  4. A recorded video interview. One take, no re-records. We verify the work history you've told us about.
  5. A short call with the founder.
  6. A paid trial of six to eight weeks doing the real job.

The trial is where the decision actually gets made, including which of the two areas you end up owning. From the first week you will be making calls on live work, and we will tell you straight how each one landed. It is paid from day one: half rate for the first two weeks while you find your feet, full rate from week three onward, and a completion payment when you finish the trial, whether or not we hire you. If we stop early, you are paid for the days you worked.

Requirements

    1. Full time once hired, and this is your only job. During the paid trial you work 4 hours a day with us, 2 of them at a fixed time inside our working day, and you can keep your current job. If you pass, you give notice and join us full time within 30 days.
    2. Reliable internet, at least 30 Mbps down and 5 Mbps up, tested live with us.
    3. Strong written English.
    4. Based in Indonesia.
    5. You track your working time with our time tracking tool from day one.

Benefits

1000 USD per month on hire, set by responsibility and demonstrated capability, not by how long you have worked.

Pass your 90-day review and your pay goes up by 50 percent. The 90 days count from the day you start full time.

On top of that:

  1. A one-month annual bonus.
  2. 15 days of paid leave a year, rising with tenure, plus your own country's public holidays.
  3. Paid sick leave.
  4. A health allowance.
  5. A coworking allowance.

Responsibility and pay move quickly here for people who earn them. Authority over decisions that reach a client moves slowly and deliberately, and it is earned on a track record rather than on a good first month. We would rather tell you that now than have you discover it in month two.

raw.excerpt: Landmark Ventures is seeking a highly motivated, resourceful, technically capable, and detail-oriented Account Executive to join the Marketing team within our Business Development Advisory practice.
raw.description:
Landmark Ventures is seeking a highly motivated, resourceful, technically capable, and detail-oriented Account Executive to join the Marketing team within our Business Development Advisory practice.

This is a high-output, execution-focused role for someone who thrives in a fast-moving environment and enjoys combining research, technology, data, AI, communication, and problem-solving.

The Account Executive will help manage outreach and marketing campaigns across multiple clients, own lead generation and prospect research, maintain high standards of data quality, and support client-facing initiatives and strategic projects, including in-person executive events.

On any given day, you may move between building a targeted prospect list, researching executives and companies, using AI tools to accelerate research and content development, managing outreach campaigns, working within CRM and prospecting platforms, responding to client requests, preparing reports, and supporting an upcoming event.

Success in this role requires more than strong communication skills. We are looking for someone who can learn quickly, leverage technology and AI effectively, execute at a high level, manage significant detail, prioritize competing deadlines, and independently solve problems without sacrificing accuracy.

Key Responsibilities:

Campaign Management & Execution
  • Manage and coordinate outreach campaigns across multiple clients and initiatives.
  • Assess markets, companies, and decision-makers based on specific client objectives.
  • Build highly targeted prospect and account lists.
  • Coordinate outreach efforts and help maximize engagement through thoughtful, effective email communication.
  • Track campaign activity and identify opportunities to improve targeting and execution.
  • Manage multiple concurrent workstreams while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.
Research & Strategic Thinking
  • Develop a strong understanding of each client's business, competitive positioning, technology, target markets, and key stakeholders.
  • Research industries, companies, executives, use cases, applications, and emerging market developments.
  • Translate broad client objectives into actionable research and prospecting strategies.
  • Connect information across different sources to identify relevant opportunities, relationships, and decision-makers.
  • Exercise judgment when information is incomplete rather than relying solely on predetermined instructions.
Lead Generation & Data Management
  • Independently identify and generate new contacts, accounts, and opportunities on behalf of clients and Landmark events.
  • Conduct executive-level prospecting using LinkedIn, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, Salesforce, and other research tools.
  • Maintain accurate, organized, and actionable prospect and campaign data.
  • Identify and resolve duplicate, incomplete, outdated, or inaccurate contact information.
  • Take ownership of data cleanliness and quality across assigned projects.
AI, LLM & Technology Proficiency
  • Demonstrate strong working proficiency with leading LLM and generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or similar platforms.
  • Use AI effectively to accelerate research, synthesize information, analyze companies and markets, develop prospecting strategies, improve written communications, and increase overall productivity.
  • Write effective prompts and iterate on AI outputs to produce accurate, useful, and contextually relevant work.
  • Understand that AI-generated output requires human judgment. Independently validate facts, identify potential errors or hallucinations, and ensure client-facing work meets Landmark's standards before use.
  • Identify opportunities to use AI, automation, and technology to improve existing workflows and increase both speed and quality of execution.
  • Become highly proficient with Landmark's technology and prospecting stack.
  • Use Excel and other tools to organize, analyze, clean, and manage prospect and campaign data.
  • Learn unfamiliar platforms and workflows quickly.
  • Independently troubleshoot routine technology, data, and workflow challenges.
Client & Team Support
  • Support strategic client projects and in-person executive events.
  • Communicate professionally and effectively with internal leadership, colleagues, clients, and senior external stakeholders.
  • Understand the nuances of client interactions and exercise sound judgment around communication and follow-through.
  • Take ownership of deliverables from initial assignment through completion.
What We're Looking For:
High-Output Execution
You are comfortable managing a significant volume of work across multiple clients and priorities. You can move quickly without allowing accuracy or attention to detail to deteriorate.

Technical & AI Aptitude
You are highly comfortable with technology and actively use AI and LLM tools to work more effectively. You understand how to use these tools to accelerate your work without outsourcing your judgment to them. When you encounter an unfamiliar platform, incomplete information, or unexpected problem, your instinct is to investigate, experiment, troubleshoot, and find a path forward.

Resourcefulness & Independent Problem-Solving
You do not need a playbook for every situation. You can take an objective, determine what information or tools you need, make reasonable decisions, and move the work forward. You know when to solve something independently and when an issue warrants escalation.

Research & Critical Thinking
You are curious and analytical. You can understand a client's business, identify relevant companies and executives, synthesize information from multiple sources, and translate broad objectives into targeted action.

Ownership & Urgency
You take responsibility for outcomes, not simply assigned tasks. You proactively identify what needs to happen next, communicate when something is at risk, and consistently follow through.

Attention to Detail
You notice things others miss. Whether reviewing contact data, evaluating AI-generated research, preparing a client deliverable, or launching an outreach campaign, you maintain a high standard for accuracy and quality.

Prioritization & Adaptability
You can calmly assess competing priorities, determine what matters most, and adjust quickly when deadlines or client needs change.

Communication & High EQ
You are an excellent written and verbal communicator who can work effectively with colleagues, clients, and senior executives. You understand nuance, communicate professionally, and know when to ask questions versus when to make a reasonable judgment and move forward.

Growth Mindset & Coachability
You welcome direct feedback, learn from mistakes, and apply what you learn. You are motivated by increasing responsibility and becoming an increasingly valuable contributor to the team.

Desired Experience & Proficiencies
  • 1 to 4 years of relevant experience in business development, account management, marketing, sales, research, client services, consulting, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated proficiency using LLMs and generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or comparable platforms in a professional or academic setting.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
  • Experience with LinkedIn and sophisticated online research is essential.
  • Experience with Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, or similar CRM and prospecting platforms is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new technologies, software, and workflows.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Experience working under tight deadlines and managing multiple simultaneous
  • priorities.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Prior SDR or traditional sales experience is not required. We place significant value on demonstrated intellectual curiosity, technical and AI aptitude, resourcefulness, execution ability, critical thinking, and attention to detail.

The Environment

Landmark is a high-energy, entrepreneurial environment where priorities can move quickly and expectations are high. This role is best suited for someone who enjoys that pace and takes pride in producing a significant volume of high-quality work. We expect our team to embrace new technology and continuously look for smarter ways to work. AI and LLMs are increasingly important tools in how we research, communicate, analyze information, and execute for clients. The expectation is not simply to use these tools, but to understand how to use them thoughtfully, efficiently, and responsibly. We believe in giving talented people opportunities to grow. Team members who demonstrate strong execution, judgment, ownership, and initiative will have opportunities to take on increasingly significant client responsibilities and contribute across the firm. We are looking for a key addition to a talented, driven, and collaborative team who wants to learn quickly, take on meaningful responsibility, and grow professionally.

About Landmark Ventures
Landmark Ventures is a strategic advisory platform operating at the intersection of investment banking, business development, and curated executive events. For more than 20 years, Landmark has worked with leading public companies, investment funds, and growth-oriented private companies.

The firm brings together deep market insight and extensive executive relationships across enterprise software, cybersecurity, IoT, industrial technology, artificial intelligence, sports, marketing technology, and digital media. A significant portion of Landmark's work involves cross-border opportunities and relationships across the United States, Europe, Asia, and Israel.

Landmark Ventures is committed to building a diverse team that brings valuable perspectives to our work. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome qualified applicants regardless of race, ethnicity, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, physical or mental ability, gender
identity or expression, or veteran status.

raw.title: Senior Researcher, Research Communication
raw.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
raw.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

We're hiring for roles that will help us scale effectively. We expect to make one or more hires from this round, including a leadership-track hire who we believe can scale to build out a new function. This role (or roles) will shape how we communicate about our research, our reasoning, our uncertainties, and our mistakes, in keeping with our commitments to transparency and rigor.

The problem this role would solve and why it matters

GiveWell's Research teams own the work of determining which grants are most cost-effective: investigating existing programs, building and revising cost-effectiveness models, commissioning research to resolve our own uncertainties, and working with implementers to develop opportunities that don't yet exist but should. Our philanthropy and communications teams own the last mile of how we talk about that work, whether through a 1:1 conversation with a donor, a donor event, or scalable communications like blog posts, newsletters, and podcasts.

Between these teams sits a question: what are the most important and accurate things we should say about our work? Answering it requires a nuanced understanding of our research and our theories of change, and it is epistemically demanding, because our external communications are held to the standards of rigor, calibration, and honesty about uncertainty that we apply to our decision-making.

Today, answering these questions runs through a small group of senior leaders. But our funding is growing, and our programs are growing with it. The volume of research we need to cover and translate keeps expanding, as does the volume of complex, sophisticated donor questions, often from people considering making very large donations to our work. The result is a new-to-us problem: producing answers that meet GiveWell’s research bar, at speed and at volume.

The hard part of this work is rarely the phrasing. It's working out what we truly believe and what communicates that most effectively to those who follow our work. This matters far beyond fundraising. Sharing our work is central to our mission: we publish our reasoning so others can challenge it, and we change our minds when the evidence demands it. We believe excellent research communications could materially shape the direction of billions of dollars in funding from GiveWell donors and other actors, potentially saving hundreds of thousands of lives.

We see this role as critical to building a new function at GiveWell. You would help us reimagine and shape the substance of what we share with our donors and the outside world.

About the role

This senior role would own GiveWell's answers to the hardest questions we get about our work. Your responsibilities would include:

  • Working out what statements our research supports, developing what we can claim and defend, testing that against the researchers who own the underlying analysis, and holding a high bar for accuracy when a simpler answer would be more convenient.
  • Prioritizing across a portfolio of questions to deliver answers at the right altitude: which questions need a fast answer with correctly conveyed uncertainty, which warrant deeper research, and which point to gaps in our communication that are best served by published research.
  • Supporting the CEO and our senior leadership in external communications and major donor engagement. A significant portion of the work, especially as this role ramps up, will support Elie Hassenfeld, our co-founder and CEO, in his direct work with our largest supporters. Over time, you would engage with donors directly on research questions.
  • Setting the standard for external communications about GiveWell's research. Some communications go directly to individual donors, but our best work builds a platform that lets us communicate more effectively with everyone: tens of thousands of donors around the world, and partner organizations who may look to our work to inform their own.
  • Producing work yourself to GiveWell’s standards of quality, including long-form write-ups explaining our research, data visualizations, and interactive tools that deepen engagement with our work. As the function scales, we expect this will extend to hiring and leading a team that produces the work. (See “Current and future team structure” below.)

Questions you might take on

More than anything else, this role is about how you engage with questions. Take, as an example, a question we often get from our donors: "How much room for more funding do you have?" We have an answer, but it isn't easy to state simply, because the question nests several others inside it: What, exactly, counts as room for more funding? Over what time frame? How much risk are we willing to take on with respect to future fundraising? Where could we be right, where could we be wrong, and what would change our view?

Answering well means knowing how to answer all of that.

Other questions you might take on include:

  • Why did GiveWell set its moral weights the way it did, and how much would changing them affect our judgments?
  • How much room for more funding does GiveWell have? How much do we need, by when, and to do what?
  • What are the best ways to increase vaccination rates in a given country?
  • Is there a cost-effectiveness bar at which a donor should prefer a peer organization to GiveWell's top charities?
  • What is GiveWell's view on emerging technologies in malaria control?
  • How are we thinking about programs like gene drives to eradicate malaria?
  • How is GiveWell taking AI into account in its grantmaking strategy?

Answering these questions well will take a range of tools and approaches that make our work easier to explain, more accessible, and more compelling to people worldwide.

As a concrete example: our cost-effectiveness models have lived in spreadsheets for years. Given the tools available and our team's capacity, that was the best way to share our work. Now, many tools could make this work much easier to engage with.

For this and other projects, the work will run the gamut:

  • Writing long, detailed research write-ups
  • Creating data visualizations and charts
  • Working with AI to build interactive tools
  • Responsively answering questions from our largest donors
  • Doing public-facing work with donor audiences, including public speaking and answering questions live

Current and future team structure

Where this role sits

This role would report to Alex Cohen, Program Director, Research, and leader of our Cross-Cutting team, and would sit within our Research team. Cross-Cutting owns the research questions that span our portfolio.

Because this function is new to GiveWell, and because it matters so much to how we deliver on our mission, this hire would also have a dotted-line relationship with Elie Hassenfeld, our co-founder and CEO, and would work closely with our Outreach teams. Beyond informing our Outreach work, this role is the entry point for big-picture questions from donors that ultimately bear on our research strategy.

Future team leadership

We may make one hire from this round, or a few. We see this work as building out a function, and we expect it to need a team and a team leader. We think that leader could come from this round. If we make a single hire, we'll weigh team leadership experience more heavily, because that person will be best positioned to grow into leading the function. If we make several hires, we expect them to join as peers at the same level, with the understanding that the team's eventual leader will likely emerge from the cohort.

Because of this, we may make hires who fit different profiles:

  • An exceptional individual contributor who matches the strengths described below. They want to do this work at the highest level, and managing people isn't what draws them in. That is a great outcome for us, as this work rewards depth, and succeeding in this role does not require wanting to manage.
  • A future team lead who has built or led a team before, or is clearly ready to. They are energized by defining a standard, hiring against it, and managing people to it. They're willing to spend their first months or longer producing excellent work with their own hands. They understand that is how they will earn the command of our research that leading this work will require.

About you

You like to understand things deeply – well enough that you can explain them simply and concretely to someone encountering them for the first time. You really like explaining ideas. It's not enough to get an answer that's satisfying to you. You're most excited when you can communicate technical ideas in plain language that helps others understand them.

You get excited about a very wide variety of questions. You're comfortable deciding which of five open questions warrants days of research, which warrants a one-pager, and which requires a fast answer with our uncertainty clearly conveyed.

You'd rather put something rough in front of a colleague after an hour to get feedback and get to a faster answer than spend a week producing something excellent alone. You bring people along in your thinking, and you are interested in getting up to speed with others' perspectives.

You like working on a variety of things. You'd much rather work on five questions over the course of a week than one question over the course of a month.

You love improving. You're more interested in getting the answer right than being right.

You're motivated by global health and development and by finding the most effective ways to improve the lives of people in low-income countries.

You're excited about leading work in a variety of mediums, whether it's long detailed write-ups, data visualizations and charts, or interactive tools.

You operate well in a matrixed environment. Most of the people whose work you depend on won't report to you, and much of your credibility will come from researchers deciding you understand their analysis well enough to speak for it. You have experience earning that kind of standing in an organization, and you're comfortable pushing back on your colleagues, being pushed back on, and holding a line when it is important.

A candidate for the future team lead role has likely built and managed a team before. They are excited to define a mandate for a new team and manage people to it while still producing excellent work themselves for as long as the role requires.

We also expect that people with the qualities below, which we look for across our Research team, will be the most successful and happy in this role.

  • GiveWell's mission and methods personally energize you. You like our approach to research, and you find personal meaning in our story of impact.
  • You're abnormally curious. You ask lots of questions, and you're willing to interrogate others' work. Your curiosity also extends to your own work: you aren't defensive when your work is scrutinized.
  • You dislike it when people express strong confidence in views that don't seem to be backed by commensurate evidence. You communicate your confidence levels carefully and legibly.
  • You love a gnarly problem. You figure out the most important questions to answer, go deep on the details where they matter (and move on where they don't), and reassess your mental models based on what you've learned.

A quantitatively oriented advanced degree is a nice-to-have rather than a must, and a lower priority than the qualities above.

Process

The process for this role will be individualized based on how familiar we already are with a candidate's work abilities in the role areas. For someone whose work we don't know well, that could mean a short call about the role, up to two paid work trials, a longer interview, and reference checks — though it may be shorter or longer depending on the candidate. We only move people to a next step when we're confident it's a good use of their time, and we aim to balance respect for that time with rigor in how we make our hiring decisions.

The details

  • Compensation: We set salaries using a location-based tier system. Our pay for this role:
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $308,000.
    • All other U.S. locations: $280,000.
    • International: Similar to the “all other U.S. locations” salary, based on historical exchange rates and delivered in locally-denominated currency. We can share a precise figure upon request after the first work trial stage.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the U.S. for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • Automatic contribution equal to 5% of your gross salary into your 403(b) retirement plan (for U.S.-based staff)
  • Location: GiveWell's staff work primarily remotely, within the U.S. and abroad. This position is eligible for fully remote work.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California; Brooklyn, New York; or London, UK. We'll cover relocation expenses for candidates who wish to move to any of our physical office locations.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis. A successful candidate will need to commit to a work schedule that has some overlap with U.S. working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Working arrangements: We're uncertain about whether non-full-time arrangements are possible and exactly how your work might develop over time — we're happy to discuss both in depth with strong candidates.
  • Visa sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we'll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Travel: Research team members are sometimes required to attend international site visits and conferences (on average 1-2 per year), with additional travel for those interested in traveling more. Additionally, we strongly encourage staff members to attend quarterly whole-org and department retreats to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. We'll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we'll accommodate staff who have conflicting family or other commitments.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

GiveWell is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer by choice. At minimum, this means that we comply with all federal, state, and local EEO and employment laws. Beyond the requirements of those laws, we value our team’s diversity in all respects, and we desire to maintain a work environment free of harassment or discrimination—we want our team members to thrive at GiveWell. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at . We will consider employment for qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that you have read and consent to GiveWell's Privacy Statement for Applicants. By completing an application exercise, you acknowledge and assent to GiveWell's Work Trial Policy.
